name: Terminal Empty-Core Obstruction Towers
statement: For every $r\ge1$, the antipodal repair tower $X_r=(G\times Q_r)\cup(\{91\}\times(Q_r\setminus\{0^r\}))\cup(\{157\}\times(Q_r\setminus\{1^r\}))$ over the certified cornerless 291-concept seed is a corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor with empty unique-midpoint core. It has isometric dimension $12+r$, exactly $293\cdot2^r-2$ concepts, and exactly $2r$ corners. For $r=1$, deleting either corner leaves a unique-midpoint core of order 76. Thus terminality restores neither the implication from empty core to peelability nor the existence of a corner whose deletion preserves empty core.
proof: The two tips have certified peelable one-concept extensions and acquire distinct four-coordinate supports. The antipodal repair-tower theorem gives ampleness, forbiddenness, order, and dimension, while the complementary punctured rows partition all signed layer facets and the terminal facet-partition theorem gives corner-descent terminality. Each punctured $r$-cube row has $r$ corners and the seed has none, so the repair-cover corner formula gives $2r$ corners. Successful-layer core separation makes the tower core empty. At $r=1$, deleting either occurrence corner removes its row; the remaining sections are the 76-core seed and an empty-core one-tip repair, so the layerwise formula gives core order 76. The archived checker independently verifies the seed and repair hashes, exact shadows, corners, static pruning orders, and core witnesses for $r=1,2$ and all their corner deletions.
